narrative.overview:
A practical neighborhood wayfinding system: forest navigation frames a pale, readable work surface. Soft green groups controls, while lime marks the discovery action. Familiar Chinese forms and clear list hierarchy help people compare real information quickly.

The visual system is code-led: system fonts, line icons, tonal panels, and native controls. No shipping raster assets are required. The useful character comes from alignment, legible labels, and honest states.
keyCharacteristics: Light, readable work surfaces within a forest-green shell.
List-first comparison with restrained line icons.
Clearly labeled controls and truthful empty, unavailable, and error states.

rules.name: The Useful Accent Rule
rules.body: Use lime for orientation and the discovery action; keep longer reading areas neutral.

dos: Do keep the search scope and recommendation reasons visibly labeled.
Do use the shared focus treatment and preserve native form semantics.
Do keep unknown prices and missing data explicit.
Do adapt filters before results on compact screens.
donts: Don't turn the application into a promotional landing page.
Don't use restaurant imagery or invented reviews to fill unavailable states.
Don't add decorative shadows or literal park-sign ornament.
Don't treat the compact screenshot as proof of a 390px phone layout.
